# Arca Swift SDK

Native Swift concurrency SDK. See README.md and the public Swift SDK reference
for the full API. Use canonical market IDs (for example hl:0:BTC), keep monetary
values as decimal strings, and preserve server authority for execution/risk.
Public source preference is optional and reversible; Arca remains the default.

## Aggregation watches and reconnects (2.12.1)

`watchAggregation` creates its watch on the socket (`create_aggregation_watch`),
not over REST. The server destroys that watch with the connection, so the SDK
re-creates it after every reconnect or rotation; the stream keeps its last value
meanwhile and retries a failed re-create with backoff. Once a connection has
authenticated, a server error rejects one request (a non-canonical market id, a
path outside the credential's scope) and never closes the socket; an error that
names a `requestId` fails only that request. The
reconnect backoff (1 s doubling to 30 s) resets only after a connection has
stayed up for 30 s, `ensureConnected()` does not cut a pending backoff short, and
returning to the foreground reconnects at once without resetting the backoff.

## Market data diagnostics (2.12.0)

`watchMarketDataDiagnostics()` observes a conflated cumulative `MarketDataDiagnostics`
snapshot: Swift returns an AsyncStream (await it); Kotlin returns a StateFlow.
`marketDataDiagnostics` reads the current snapshot (await in Swift). Observation
adds no socket, subscription or polling timer. Updates accompany traffic at most
once a second plus source/interest/connection transitions. Cancel observation to
release it. Use foreground-window deltas, not number of diagnostic callbacks.

Fields: elapsedMs, preference, requestedPriceMarkets, directSubscriptions,
arcaServingMarkets/hyperliquidServingMarkets (last routed quote source),
arcaPriceValues/hyperliquidPriceValues, arcaCandleFrames/hyperliquidCandleFrames,
hyperliquidFailures/hyperliquidRecoveries/hyperliquidRecoveryMs,
arcaConnected/arcaDisconnects, arcaPayloadBytes/hyperliquidPayloadBytes, firstPriceMs.
Counters last for one SDK client and include reconnects. Deliberate disconnects
can increment Arca disconnects; split lifecycle windows. Intentional suspension
cancels a pending direct-recovery duration. All bytes are incoming application
payloads, excluding framing/TLS; Arca's count includes its shared account socket.
The first price delay starts at socket-manager creation and concerns the first
routed interested price. It is not venue latency. Quiet prices are not failures,
no exchange timestamp is invented, and Arca still owns finalized candles.

## Scoped projection watches and interest-scoped mids (2.13.0)

`watchProjection(name:paths:prefix:exchange:)` watches a registered projection
for the accounts named: `paths` (max 500 exact object paths) and/or a `prefix`
sub-tree, both intersected with the projection's registered resources (a path
outside them is dropped; they compose as AND). The server reply is the scope's
snapshot (a path set whole; a prefix scope's first page, the rest fetched over
REST with the same prefix). `setPaths(_:)` / `setPrefix(_:)` replace the scope
in place under the same watch id (`update_projection_watch`; the ack carries the
new scope's snapshot, which replaces the rows; a later call supersedes an
earlier one); `scope` is the current interest set. A watch with no `paths` and
no `prefix` is EMPTY — it delivers nothing until `setPaths` names a set — and
never means every covered account; a client that wants the whole projection
passes the projection's own prefix (on a realm-wide projection, the shape to
avoid on a device). Frames are per-account deltas (`removed` drops rows); the
stream re-marks rows against mids between deltas, subscribing to mids only for
the markets its rows hold; reconnects and rotations re-create the watch with
the current scope. Requires `arca:ReadProjection` on the projection name.
`getProjectionValuations(name:prefix:path:paths:cursor:limit:)` is the REST read
with the same narrowing.

`watchPrices(exchange:markets:)`: the market list is the stream's price interest
on BOTH providers. The direct Hyperliquid source subscribes one `bbo` per market;
the Arca socket's `subscribe_mids` carries the union of every live consumer's
markets (`watchPrices`, `watchExchangeState`, `watchObject`, `watchAggregation`,
`watchProjection` all declare the markets their positions hold), is re-sent when
the union changes (widening at once, narrowing after the release debounce) and
is replayed on reconnect. `setMarkets` changes a stream's set in place. Only an
unscoped `watchPrices()` (empty list) asks the server for every market. A market
no earlier consumer asked for is not in the retained snapshot yet; it lands with
the snapshot the widened subscription triggers, one round trip after return.
Driving the manager directly: `acquireMids(exchange:allMarkets:)` /
`releaseMids(allMarkets:)` are the refcounts (default `true` keeps the old
all-markets meaning); a bare `subscribeMids` / `unsubscribeMids` pair is left
alone by them. Measured from 2026-10-17 02:32 UTC on production (payload
bytes, 5 min): one market 0.02 KiB/s, a 22-market board 1.1 KiB/s (7.8
frames/s), every market (567 ids) 6.2 KiB/s, versus Hyperliquid `bbo` on the
same 22 markets 7.8 KiB/s (57 frames/s) and `allMids` 4.8 KiB/s;
`marketDataDiagnostics` reports `arcaPayloadBytes` / `hyperliquidPayloadBytes`
per client.
